title: Maximum-Entropy Extension of Quantum Correlation Functions from Short Real-Time Dynamics
authors: Filippo Maria Gambetta, Sabrina Yue Wang, Raul A. Santos
abstract: Correlation functions are central to understanding the behavior of quantum systems, with their spectra giving direct access to quasiparticle and collective excitations. However, the long-time evolution required for sufficient spectral resolution is challenging to reach for both classical and quantum simulations. In this work, we introduce a principled approach for extending time series of quantum correlation functions and reconstructing their spectral densities, based on their connection with covariance sequences of stationary stochastic processes. This connection enables us to apply Burg's maximum-entropy principle to find the least-committal extension compatible with the measured values of the correlation function, which corresponds to an all-pole autoregressive model whose coefficients solve a set of Yule--Walker equations. The resulting extension is positive semi-definite by construction, guaranteeing the positivity of the spectrum and the automatic satisfaction of its total spectral weight sum rule. The approach applies to both scalar and matrix-valued correlation functions, including those with highly structured or continuous spectra. The generalization to the matrix case makes it possible to trade simulation time for additional measured correlation functions, enabling accurate time-series extension and spectral reconstruction from short-time data, even in the presence of noise.
summary: This paper introduces a maximum-entropy framework to reconstruct the spectral density of quantum correlation functions from limited real-time measurements. By modeling the correlation function as a stationary stochastic process, it applies Burg's principle to find the least-committal, positive semi-definite extension. This method offers a significant improvement over traditional techniques, enabling accurate spectral analysis even when data is noisy or the spectrum is continuous.
main_problem: The core problem is reconstructing the spectral density of quantum correlation functions from limited, short-time real-time dynamics data.
main_result: The authors propose a maximum-entropy extension method that guarantees a positive semi-definite spectrum and satisfies fundamental sum rules, significantly improving upon standard linear prediction techniques.
method: The method treats the correlation function as a covariance sequence of a stationary stochastic process and applies Burg's maximum-entropy principle, modeling the extension via an all-pole autoregressive (AR) or Vector AR (VAR) model.
model_or_system: The theory applies to general quantum many-body systems, using time-dependent correlation functions, such as those related to Green's functions or dynamical structure factors.
key_observables: Time-dependent correlation functions g(t), the spectral density S(omega), and the associated Gram matrix R(n).
important_parameters: The length of the measured time series (n), the order of the AR model (p), and the noise level.
main_assumptions: The underlying process is assumed to be a Wide-Sense Stationary (WSS) stochastic process, and the method relies on the Gram matrix being positive semi-definite.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the spectral reconstruction problem and limitations of existing methods (LP, Prony) to introducing the maximum-entropy approach for both scalar and matrix correlation functions, culminating in detailed mathematical derivations for the VAR model and denoising techniques.
why_interesting: This work provides a robust, mathematically principled tool for extracting spectral information from noisy, short-time quantum dynamics data, which is crucial for analyzing transport and excitation spectra in condensed matter systems.
